disclaimer.audience: AEPD innovation lab / technical due diligence
disclaimer.text_es: Este documento es una EIPD de arquitectura de referencia para un laboratorio de innovación. No constituye una notificación a la autoridad de control ni una consulta previa del artículo 36 RGPD. El conjunto de datos de demostración es el de la competición Kaggle Porto Seguro (variables anonimizadas ps_*). Un responsable real que trate datos personales identificables para suscripción debería elaborar y firmar su propia EIPD sobre su tratamiento.
disclaimer.text_en: This document is a reference-architecture EIPD / DPIA for an innovation lab. It is not a notification to the supervisory authority and not a GDPR Article 36 prior consultation. The demonstration dataset is the Porto Seguro Kaggle competition (anonymized ps_* features). A real controller that processes identifiable personal data for underwriting should draft and sign its own DPIA on that processing.

controller_hypothetical.name: Porto Seguro Compliance Hub (demo controller)
controller_hypothetical.note: Hypothetical for the lab walkthrough. No live insurance book is processed here.

roles.processor: none in this demo (single local stack)

processing_description.name: Insurance claim probability scoring (underwriting decision support)
purposes: Estimate P(claim) for a policyholder record to support underwriting and portfolio risk review
Produce native glass-box explanations for a human reviewer
Emit audit evidence (metrics, bias proxies, drift, artifact hashes)
out_of_scope: Fully automated rejection of a contract without human review (production must not do this)
Processing of special-category data (Art. 9) — not collected in this demo
processing_description.data_subjects: In production: policyholders and applicants. In this demo: no identifiable natural persons; Kaggle anonymized tabular rows.

data_categories.sensitive_proxies: Engineered frequency encodings and regional products may correlate with socio-economic or geographic groups; audited as proxies, not as protected attributes.

processing_description.recipients: Local Streamlit / FastAPI demo operators only. No third-country transfer in this stack.
processing_description.retention: Demo artifacts retained for reproducibility (model pkl, SHA-256 sidecars, JSON packs). Production must define a retention schedule (Art. 5(1)(e)).

demo.position: If the competition dataset is irreversibly anonymised (Recital 26 GDPR), the GDPR does not apply to those records. This EIPD is still maintained as the template a controller would need when the same pipeline processes personal data.

candidate_bases: Art. 6(1)(b) — performance of an insurance contract / pre-contractual steps
Art. 6(1)(f) — legitimate interests of the insurer in risk selection, subject to balancing test and Art. 21 objection
production_analogue.not_used_here: No production legal basis is asserted for this repository.

why_dpia_is_required.article_35_1: Processing likely to result in a high risk to rights and freedoms — production analogue: large-scale scoring of applicants.
why_dpia_is_required.article_35_3_a: Systematic and extensive evaluation of personal aspects based on automated processing, including profiling, on which decisions are based that produce legal effects or similarly significantly affect the person (underwriting / pricing analogue).
why_dpia_is_required.aepd_list: Insurance scoring / profiling of applicants is the type of processing typically covered by the AEPD list of treatments requiring an EIPD. Confirm against the current published list before any live filing.
why_dpia_is_required.demo_nuance: This repository does not take automated legal decisions on real people. The EIPD exists so the lab can inspect the control design that would sit in front of such a decision.

necessity_and_proportionality.purpose_limitation_art_5_1_b: Single purpose: claim-probability decision support and compliance evidence. Not reused for marketing or unrelated profiling in this stack.
necessity_and_proportionality.data_minimisation_art_5_1_c: No names, contact data, national ID, or Art. 9 attributes ingested. Features are already hashed/anonymized by the dataset publisher. Pipeline does not re-identify.
necessity_and_proportionality.accuracy_art_5_1_d: Hold-out ROC-AUC ~0.639 (realistic for this imbalance). Threshold tuned on train only. Accuracy ~87% is not used as a success metric.
necessity_and_proportionality.storage_limitation_art_5_1_e: Demo: artifacts for audit replay. Production: define deletion aligned with insurance retention law.
necessity_and_proportionality.integrity_confidentiality_art_5_1_f: SHA-256 sidecars on model and feature-engineer pickles; Docker read-only artifact mount; no secrets in the demo repo.
necessity_and_proportionality.accountability_art_5_2: JSON evidence packs, Streamlit Model Card, audit_results.json, this DPIA pack.

data_subject_rights.information_art_13_14: Model Card + this DPIA describe purpose, logic (EBM additive terms), and human review. Production privacy notice would cite this pack.
data_subject_rights.access_art_15_1_h: Meaningful information about the logic involved, and the significance and envisaged consequences of such processing (Art. 15(1)(h)) — native EBM log-odds contributions, not Art. 22(3).
data_subject_rights.rectification_art_16: Feature pipeline is deterministic from input row; correction is a data-quality process upstream.
data_subject_rights.erasure_art_17: Demo has no identity index. Production must support deletion of scores and training copies where legally required.
data_subject_rights.objection_art_21: Production legitimate-interest scoring must honour objection. Demo does not run a live objection channel.

automated_decisions_art_22.position: Art. 22(3) safeguards (human intervention, express a view, contest) apply where Art. 22(2)(a) or (c) is the basis. Logic/significance of the decision is Art. 15(1)(h), not Art. 22(3).
implementation_in_this_repo: Model output is advisory (Art. 22 analogue: human review routing)
Native EBM local contributions implement Art. 15(1)(h)-style logic information
Contestability requires an operational process the demo does not run

risk_register.risk: Unfair scoring via geographic or behavioural proxies although Art. 9 attributes are not collected
mitigations: Proxy bias audit on ps_ind_03, ps_reg_03, ps_car_13 (demographic parity / equal opportunity)

risk_register.risk: Data drift silently degrades a subgroup and changes claim scores
mitigations: KS / PSI drift monitor (Art. 9 EU AI Act analogue)
Shadow monitor off the hot path

risk_register.risk: Residual re-identification if a production extract were joined with external files
Over-reliance on the score (automation bias) without contestability
mitigations: Glass-box local explanations on log-odds scale

risk_register.risk: Integrity failure (wrong or tampered model artifact in production)
mitigations: SHA-256 sidecars for ebm_model_v1.pkl and feature_engineer_v1.pkl

residual_risk_summary.scale_note: Scores are Porto Seguro likelihood × severity (1–5), NOT an AEPD official scale. Residual figures in this static pack are estimates pending linked controls with verification_state tested|verified. The runtime engine will not lower residual without that evidence.
residual_risk_summary.article_36: Prior consultation with the AEPD is not triggered by this demonstration. A live controller would reassess residual high risk after mitigations before any Art. 36 filing.

mitigations_in_code.control: Anonymized feature set; no Art. 9 attributes
Polars last-millisecond bridge (no extra copies of identity data)

gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.this_repo: Anonymized Kaggle schema; Polars validation; train-only feature engineer fit

gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.gdpr: Art. 15(1)(h) logic and consequences; Art. 22(3) HITL/contest (not the logic itself)
gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.this_repo: Native EBM explain_local / explain_global; Model Card
Advisory scores; threshold routing to underwriter review

gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.gdpr: Art. 5(1)(d) accuracy; Art. 32 security of processing
gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.this_repo: Hold-out metrics; adversarial tests; SHA-256; read-only mounts

gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.eu_ai_act: Art. 9 risk management; Annex IV technical documentation
gdpr_eu_ai_act_crosswalk.this_repo: This pack + eu_ai_act_conformity_v1.json + Streamlit evidence pages

applicability_and_anonymisation.applicability_rationale: The demo file uses publisher-anonymised Kaggle columns (ps_*). A publisher description is not a Recital 26 finding that the information is anonymous. Identifiability, including means reasonably likely to be used, has not been tested. GDPR applicability for this file remains unknown.
gaps: No re-identification test or Recital 26 analysis is on record.
Publisher anonymisation must not be treated as GDPR non-applicability.
next_actions: Controller (not this software) must determine whether the dataset is anonymous information or personal data.
If the same pipeline is used on identifiable records, treat that as a distinct processing operation.

roles_and_accountability.applicability_rationale: No controller, processor, or DPO is appointed in this repository. Labels in the static EIPD pack are hypothetical demo actors, not legal appointments.
gaps: Controller identity is not established (owner is null).
Processor inventory is not a signed Art. 28 record.
DPO designation (Art. 37) is not evidenced.
next_actions: A real operator must name controller, contact point, and whether a DPO is required.
Do not treat demo role strings as appointments.

purposes_and_lawful_basis.applicability_rationale: Intended demo purpose is claim-probability decision support. No Art. 6 basis is selected. Consent is not used as a default. Art. 9 is not determined merely because special-category column names are absent.
gaps: Art. 6 lawful basis is unknown / to_be_determined.
No documented balancing test or contract-necessity analysis.
Art. 9 condition is not assessed for a live insurance book.
next_actions: Controller must select and justify an Art. 6 basis for any identifiable processing.
Do not default to consent for underwriting or claims scoring.

findings.intended_purpose_demo: Estimate P(claim) to support a human reviewer; emit explanations and technical evidence.

data_inventory_and_minimisation.applicability_rationale: Demo inventory is the Kaggle schema (ps_ind/ps_reg/ps_car/ps_calc). Necessity of each variable for a live purpose is not evidenced. Fairness screening uses proxy columns; those metrics are not GDPR evidence and this block does not collect or infer protected attributes.
gaps: No signed data inventory or necessity review per variable.
Recipients and sources for a production deployment are not documented.
next_actions: Map categories, sources, recipients, and retention to the live purpose.
Keep fairness proxies out of any protected-attribute collection process.

fairness_audit_inputs.note: Technical bias metrics must not be reused as Art. 5(1)(a) or non-discrimination proof.

transparency.applicability_rationale: The Model Card and EIPD pack describe the demo system. They are not an Art. 12–14 privacy notice to data subjects of a live controller.
gaps: No production privacy notice (Arts. 13–14) is on record.
Layered notice, language, and timing of information are not evidenced.
next_actions: Draft and approve notices against the live purpose, recipients, and rights.

data_subject_rights.applicability_rationale: No operational procedure exists to receive or fulfil data-subject requests. Native EBM explanations are technical artefacts analogous to Art. 15(1)(h) logic information; they are not a rights-handling process.
gaps: No request channel, identity verification, or fulfilment SLA is documented.
Erasure, objection, and portability procedures are missing.
next_actions: Document procedures and keep proof of handling for each applicable right.

automated_decision_making.applicability_rationale: Art. 22 applicability is not determined. Advisory design and a human reviewer do not, by themselves, prove that Art. 22 does not apply. Exclusive automation, legal or similarly significant effects, and effective human intervention remain untested.
gaps: No assessment of legal or similarly significant effects for a live underwriting/pricing/claims decision.
Human intervention is a design claim; effectiveness is not tested.
Art. 22(3) safeguards (intervention, express a view, contest) are not operationally evidenced.
next_actions: Assess Art. 22 against the live decision, not against the presence of a UI reviewer.
If Art. 22 applies, evidence the Art. 22(2) condition and Art. 22(3) safeguards.

privacy_by_design_and_default.applicability_rationale: Repository design choices (competition schema, no Art. 9 column names, train-only feature fit) are not an Art. 25 programme for a live controller.
gaps: No Art. 25 risk-based measure register tied to a live purpose.
Default settings for a production service are not evidenced.
next_actions: Document Art. 25 measures against the actual processing, then test them.

security_of_processing.applicability_rationale: Code contains integrity checksums (SHA-256 sidecars) and a local audit hash chain. Those artefacts are not a tested Art. 32 control set (no WORM, no KMS, no security test report).
gaps: No Art. 32 test report, penetration test, or residual-risk acceptance by the controller.
Local JSONL hash chain is not immutable storage.
next_actions: Commission security testing appropriate to a live personal-data processing.

retention_and_deletion.applicability_rationale: Demo artifacts are kept for reproducibility. No justified retention schedule, deletion procedure, or backup-expiry control is on record.
gaps: Retention period is to_be_determined.
Deletion and backup erasure procedures are missing.
next_actions: Define retention aligned with the live purpose and insurance record-keeping law, then evidence deletion.

dpia.legal_reference: GDPR Art. 35; Art. 36; EDPB WP248 rev.01
dpia.applicability_rationale: A demonstration EIPD pack and a screening workspace exist. They are not a signed Art. 35 decision and not an Art. 36 prior consultation. Publisher anonymisation does not remove the need to screen a live identifiable processing.
gaps: Art. 35 decision is unsigned; residual scores in the static pack are estimated pending verification.
DPO consultation (Art. 35(2)) is not evidenced.
next_actions: For identifiable production processing, complete screening, EIPD, and residual-risk review.
Flag Art. 36 only if residual high risk remains after mitigations — not because this demo exists.

processors_and_transfers.applicability_rationale: This local demo stack does not configure a processor contract or a third-country transfer. That observation is not a finding that Art. 28 or Chapter V are not applicable to a live deployment.
gaps: No Art. 28 contracts, SCCs, or transfer assessments are on record.
Hosting, logging, and model-vendor roles for production are unknown.
next_actions: Inventory processors and international transfers before any live personal-data processing.

records_and_incident_response.applicability_rationale: Control-plane JSONL is a technical audit log, not an Art. 30 record of processing. No Arts. 33–34 incident procedure is evidenced.
gaps: Art. 30 record of processing activities is missing.
Personal-data breach detection, 72-hour notification, and data-subject communication procedures are missing.
next_actions: Maintain Art. 30 records where required and rehearse Arts. 33–34 procedures.
